deals.debtNotes: Not part of the assumable Guggenheim loan pool. The $100,441,000 / 5.25% / Nov-2032 assumable financing encumbers a nine-asset subset (Brickyard Plaza, Fairview Commons, Gold Star Plaza, Golden Triangle, Hamburg Square, Pine Grove Plaza, Southington Center, Trexler Mall, Washington Center Shoppes) - Tampa Festival is unencumbered.
deals.proximityHighways: Frontage on East Hillsborough Avenue (41,500 VPD), positioned 1.3 miles from the Hillsborough Avenue interchange with Interstate 275 (176,000 VPD) in infill Tampa.
deals.retailCotenants: Competing centers in the immediate corridor include Eastgate Shopping Center, Hillsboro Plaza, Northgate Shopping Center and Magic Mall. Nearby demand drivers include NetPark Tampa Bay, Tampa's largest corporate office campus at 1 million SF across 98 acres, and City Center at Hanna Avenue, a $108 million, 161,000 SF municipal complex built in 2023. Rogers Park Golf Course adjoins the trade area.

marketDemographics.source: Project Evergreen property OM (CBRE), Demographics page - 2025 current-year estimates
marketDemographics.note: The densest trade area in Project Evergreen: 325,293 residents within five miles and 488,862 across the true trade area at $104,637 average household income, with a daytime population of 679,589 - roughly 1.4x the residential population, reflecting the infill Tampa employment base. Population is growing steadily at 1.12% annually within five miles with households up 1.25% annually, and average household income is projected to rise 15-18% by 2030. Income rises sharply with distance from the center ($74,936 at one mile to $104,637 across the trade area), so the immediate ring is materially poorer than the draw area.

deals.notes: Tampa Festival is a 141,580 SF community center on approximately 14.8 acres fronting East Hillsborough Avenue (41,500 VPD) 1.3 miles from Interstate 275 in infill Tampa, built in 1965 and renovated in 2012. It is reported as 100% leased, and that figure needs three large caveats before it means anything. First, BOTH RAINBOW STORES - 16,800 SF, 11.9% of the GLA - pay ZERO base rent and ZERO expense reimbursements: their co-tenancy clauses have already been triggered and CBRE's model states they pay co-tenancy rent of 4% of gross sales UNTIL FULL LEASE EXPIRATION, meaning the relief does not cure. That produces $87,654 of percentage rent in place of what would otherwise be roughly $200,000 of base rent plus recoveries, and their renewal options carry the same $0 base rent structure. Second, RENT-A-CENTER VACATED IN APRIL 2026 and is dark, though it continues to pay $64,464 a year through April 2030 - 4,800 SF of physically empty space counted as occupied. Third, Key Foods (35,600 SF, 25.1% of GLA) and The Juice Bar (6,814 SF) are both GROSS leases paying no recoveries at all. Between the two Rainbows, Key Foods and The Juice Bar, 59,214 SF - 41.8% of the building - contributes nothing toward CAM, taxes or insurance, which is why only $388,356 of the center's $730,611 operating expense load is recovered, a 53% recovery ratio that is the weakest in the portfolio. In-place base rent from the 9/1/2026 rent roll is $1,339,066, or $9.46 PSF, and CBRE's in-place NOI is $1,091,172 on $1,821,784 of effective gross revenue. Against that, the location is genuinely good: the densest trade area in Project Evergreen at 325,293 residents within five miles and 488,862 across the trade area at $104,637 average income, a 679,589 daytime population, and Key Foods ranking in the top 46% of its chain nationally by foot traffic. CBRE frames the asset as a value-add and land-bank play - 57% of GLA rolls during a ten-year hold, and the 14.8-acre infill site could be densified with residential or mixed use. That is a credible thesis, but the near-term arithmetic is that 15,159 SF of Citi Trends rolls in October 2027 and 9,750 SF of dialysis centre - 13.5% of all base rent - rolls in June 2027, both within months of a 2027 closing.
keyAssumptions: SOURCES: roster built from the WHLR MRI rent roll dated 9/1/2026 (authoritative for current tenant, suite, SF, rent, dates and contractual steps); options, recovery methods, CAM caps, co-tenancy status, the dark-tenant disclosure, reported sales and occupancy-cost health ratios from the CBRE Argus model Project Evergreen_FL_Tampa Festival (FINAL).xlsx dated 8/21/2026; historical income and expense from the WHLR income statement for the 12 months ended December 2025 (entity WHLRTF); assessed value and tax detail from the Argus assumptions page; demographics, traffic counts, parking count, Placer.ai chain ranking and property description from the property OM.

ROSTER TIE-OUT: 22 leases sum to 141,580 SF, exactly the rent roll's stated GLA (0 SF vacant, 100.0% occupied). Monthly base rent sums to $111,588.87, exactly the roll's printed total; annualized = $1,339,066. Two of those 22 leases (both Rainbow stores) carry $0 base rent.

OCCUPANCY IS 100% ONLY IN A LEGAL SENSE: 16,800 SF (11.9%) pays no base rent under triggered co-tenancy clauses and 4,800 SF (3.4%) is physically dark though still paying. Economically the center behaves closer to 85% leased with a rent-paying vacancy on top.

HEADLINE NOI BASIS: noi / effectiveGrossIncome / operatingExpenses are CBRE's published In-Place Pro-Forma for calendar 2027 ($1,821,784 EGR less $730,611 of operating expense = $1,091,172, a $1 rounding difference), which is the basis behind the OM's stated in-place NOI. The VDR portfolio table rounds this to $1,090,000. EGR includes $87,654 of Rainbow co-tenancy percentage rent and $1,200 of Speedwash signage income.

RECOVERIES BASIS: nnnRecoveries of $376,375 and the per-tenant expenseReimbursements are CBRE's in-place figures and combine BOTH the operating-expense recovery and the separately-stated real estate tax recovery. CBRE's published total is $388,356; the per-tenant table sums to $376,375, leaving $11,981 that CBRE does not allocate by tenant. The rent roll's monthly cost-recovery column totals $367,598 annualized.

GPR RECONCILIATION: grossPotentialRent of $1,339,066 is the 9/1/2026 roll's in-place base rent and ties to the roster. CBRE's in-place pro-forma base rent of $1,344,574 is $5,508 higher because it runs contractual steps landing during calendar 2027.

THE OM SITE PLAN SHOWS BLENDED, NOT CONTRACT, RENT: Citi Trends reads $5.49 PSF on the site plan against a $6.59 contract rent (CBRE's figure is ten months of a lease expiring 10/31/2027); H&R Block reads $23.18 against $22.50; T-Mobile $26.19 against $25.63; Golden Krust $22.00 against $21.50. The roster carries CONTRACT rent from the rent roll throughout.

SPEEDWASH TERM - MODELED, NOT CONTRACTED: the OM site plan shows Dec-37 and CBRE's model runs the lease to 12/31/2037. CBRE's own note states the CURRENT LEASE EXPIRATION IS 12/31/2027 and that it modeled a 10-year renewal based on ongoing assignment discussions with the tenant. leaseExpiry carries the contractual 12/31/2027 date. This also means CBRE's reported WALT is inflated - excluding the modeled extension, WALT is 4.17 years as of 9/1/2026, consistent with CBRE's own rent-roll tab figure of 4.12 as of 1/1/2027.

WALT: the OM's headline of approximately 7.8 years is the ANCHOR WALT from the VDR portfolio table, not the full-roster figure. Full-roster WALT weighted by SF on contractual expiries is 4.17 years as of 9/1/2026.

ACTUAL vs IN-PLACE: the owner's YE-2025 income statement shows actual NOI of $1,006,554 on $1,946,954 of total income and $940,400 of operating expense. Note the 2025 statement books $300,000 of Base Rent Gross (Key Foods and The Juice Bar), $4,955 of Base Rent Cotenancy and $81,712 of Percentage Rent Cotenancy (the two Rainbow stores) - independent confirmation of the co-tenancy structure. Actual operating expense of $940,400 is $209,789 HIGHER than CBRE's $730,611 model, driven largely by $137,655 of billable non-CAM third-party charges and $165,385 of total non-CAM operating expense that CBRE strips out; underwrite the expense load carefully.

TAXES: the Argus assumptions page discloses a 2025 assessed value of $13,182,533, 2025 ad valorem taxes of $251,522 and non-ad-valorem assessments of $25,849 - together $277,371, which ties to the YE-2025 income statement's Real Estate Tax Expense of $277,379. CBRE explicitly did NOT reassess and modeled taxes at 2026 budgeted amounts. Florida resets non-homestead commercial property to just value on a qualifying change of ownership, so a purchase materially above the current assessment steps taxes up. CBRE also did NOT adjust insurance, holding 2026 budget at $0.44 PSF property and $0.18 PSF liability - Tampa windstorm exposure means a buyer's own program could differ substantially.

SALES BASIS: salesPSF and occupancyCost are CBRE's In-Place Pro-Forma reported sales and health ratios. Eight tenants report; the rest are null rather than estimated. The Rainbow stores' sales matter more than usual because their entire rent is 4% of those sales.

LEASE CLAUSES ARE OM-SOURCED, NOT ABSTRACTED: the co-tenancy status, dark-tenant disclosure, CAM caps and recovery structures recorded in tenant notes come from CBRE's Argus lease summaries, not from executed lease documents. The Rainbow co-tenancy clauses in particular must be read in full - what triggered them, whether they can cure, and what the landlord's remedies are - before any re-tenanting or mark-to-market case is underwritten.
NO PRICING: the portfolio is marketed unpriced, so askingPrice, capRate and pricePerSF are null rather than estimated.

redFlags.description: BOTH RAINBOW LEASES ARE ON TRIGGERED CO-TENANCY RENT AND PAY ZERO BASE RENT. Rainbow USA (11,000 SF, suite 165) and Rainbow Women & Kids (5,800 SF, suite 121) together hold 16,800 SF, 11.9% of the GLA, and pay NO base rent and NO expense reimbursements. CBRE's model states each pays co-tenancy rent of 4% of all gross sales UNTIL FULL LEASE EXPIRATION - the relief does not appear to cure even though Key Foods is now open. That produces $87,654 of percentage rent in place of roughly $200,000 of base rent plus recoveries at CBRE's $10.00-$12.00 PSF junior-anchor market. Worse, the modeled renewal options for BOTH stores also carry $0 base rent at 4% of sales. Read these clauses in full: what triggered them, whether Key Foods' opening cures them, and what the landlord can do about it is the single most valuable diligence question at this asset.

RENT-A-CENTER IS DARK. CBRE's model states the tenant VACATED IN APRIL 2026 but continues to pay rent - 4,800 SF, 3.4% of GLA, $64,464 a year at $13.43 PSF running to 4/30/2030. It holds one remaining 5-year option at $14.77 PSF which CBRE does NOT model, and CBRE assigns a 0% renewal probability. The income is contractual and continues, but this is physically empty space counted inside the 100% occupancy figure, it contributes nothing to the center's traffic, and there is no landlord recapture right disclosed. Confirm whether the lease has been assigned, whether a go-dark or recapture right exists, and whether the guarantor is good for the remaining term.

41.8% of the building contributes ZERO expense recoveries. Key Foods (35,600 SF) and The Juice Bar (6,814 SF) are both GROSS leases with no recovery at all, and the two Rainbow stores (16,800 SF) pay no reimbursements under their co-tenancy relief. That is 59,214 SF. Only $388,356 of the center's $730,611 operating expense load is recovered - a 53% recovery ratio and the weakest in Project Evergreen. Every dollar of expense inflation on that 41.8% falls straight to the owner, and Key Foods' four options carry the gross structure to September 2054.

13.5% of base rent rolls in June 2027, within months of a closing. The Dialysis Center (Bio-Medical Applications, a Fresenius entity, 9,750 SF) pays $180,375 a year - the second-largest rent at the center - and expires 6/30/2027. It holds two 5-year options at $18.96 and $21.45 PSF which CBRE assumes are exercised. Add Citi Trends (15,159 SF, $99,929, expires 10/31/2027, one option at $7.00 PSF) and H&R Block (1,536 SF, 4/30/2027) and 26,445 SF representing roughly 21% of base rent is at the mercy of option elections in the first year of ownership.

Shoetime Hillsboro reports a 21.2% occupancy cost - 3,900 SF at $15.00 PSF on sales of $97 PSF. That is roughly double a sustainable footwear threshold and the lease expires 12/31/2028 with no options recorded. City Nails (11.6%), Citi Trends (10.6%) and Top China (9.4%) are also elevated. The blended reported health ratio across the eight reporting tenants is 6.65%, which is acceptable, but the distribution is wide and the weak end is concentrated in the shop line.

Actual operating expenses run $209,789 above CBRE's model. The YE-2025 statement shows $940,400 of total operating expense against CBRE's $730,611 in-place figure. The gap sits mostly in non-CAM items CBRE strips out - $137,655 of billable non-CAM third-party charges, $16,187 of non-CAM water and sewer, and a $97,333 cost-reimbursement allocation versus CBRE's $54,268 modeled management fee. Some of that is genuinely billable back to tenants, but with 41.8% of the GLA on gross or co-tenancy leases, a meaningful share is not. Rebuild the expense stack from the actuals before accepting the modeled NOI.

Key Foods is a gross lease at $7.08 PSF with options to 2054. The anchor holds 25.1% of GLA on a GROSS lease - no CAM, no tax, no insurance recovery - with a single step to $7.43 PSF in October 2029 and FOUR 5-year options running to September 2054 at a maximum of $9.04 PSF. CBRE marks the space at $8.00 PSF NNN. The tenant ranks in the top 46% of its chain nationally by foot traffic, so the income is likely durable, but on a gross structure the owner absorbs every dollar of expense growth on a quarter of the building for the next 28 years.

Florida reassessment on sale and windstorm insurance are both unmodeled. The 2025 assessed value is $13,182,533 against $277,371 of total taxes ($2.08 PSF, the largest single expense line). CBRE explicitly did NOT reassess taxes and did NOT adjust insurance, holding both at 2026 budget and stating it is the investor's responsibility. In a Tampa infill location where the OM itself argues the land is worth more than the improvements, a reassessment to a densification-supported basis could be significant.

The oldest asset in the portfolio - built in 1965 with a 2012 renovation. The YE-2025 statement shows $89,415 of repairs and maintenance including $43,514 of plumbing and $19,762 of other exterior work, plus $13,174 of fencing and $40,975 of security contract. Only $2,825 of roof spend. Order a property condition assessment and understand the deferred maintenance position, particularly plumbing and roof.

The one-mile ring is materially poorer than the draw area - $74,936 average household income within one mile against $104,637 across the true trade area, and a $53,141 median at one mile. That supports the value-oriented merchandising in place (Rainbow, Citi Trends, Family Dollar, Key Foods) but constrains how far shop rents can be pushed on rollover, which is precisely what CBRE's 49% NOI growth case depends on.

upsideItems.item: Fix the Rainbow co-tenancy - the largest single value lever in the portfolio
upsideItems.detail: 16,800 SF currently produces $87,654 of percentage rent instead of base rent. At CBRE's $10.00-$12.00 PSF junior-anchor market rents, that space would carry roughly $185,000 of base rent plus another $60,000-plus of expense recoveries - a swing of well over $150,000 of NOI, on a center whose entire in-place NOI is $1,091,172. Whether that is capturable depends entirely on the co-tenancy language: if Key Foods' opening cures the failure, rent should restore; if the clauses run to expiration as CBRE states, the opportunity arrives at the 1/31/2028 expirations. Either way this is the first thing to underwrite, and it is worth real diligence dollars to get right.

upsideItems.item: Land bank and densification on 14.8 infill acres
upsideItems.detail: CBRE explicitly frames the asset as a land-bank opportunity offered below replacement cost, with the 14.8-acre site suited to residential or mixed-use densification. The location supports it: 325,293 people within five miles, a 679,589 daytime population, direct frontage on a 41,500 VPD arterial 1.3 miles from I-275, and NetPark Tampa Bay (1 million SF across 98 acres) plus a new $108 million municipal complex nearby. With 57% of GLA rolling within ten years and a 1965-vintage building, the improvements are not the constraint on what the site can become.

upsideItems.item: Genuine mark-to-market across a roster that is 26% below market
upsideItems.detail: In-place rent averages $9.46 PSF against CBRE's blended market. The gaps are large and concentrated in space that rolls: J-Lo Beauty Supply at $5.34 vs $10.00, Family Dollar $7.23 vs $10.00, Citi Trends $6.59 vs $10.00, The Juice Bar $7.04 vs $12.00, Shoetime $15.00 vs $12.00 (above), Rent-A-Center $13.43 vs $12.00. CBRE projects 49% NOI growth over ten years and a 4.05% CAGR on this basis. Unlike the locked-anchor assets elsewhere in the portfolio, most of this gap sits in leases with short terms or single options rather than 20-year chains.

upsideItems.item: The densest, highest-income trade area in Project Evergreen
upsideItems.detail: 325,293 residents within five miles and 488,862 across the true trade area at $104,637 average household income, with 679,589 daytime population - roughly 1.4x residential, reflecting the infill Tampa employment base. Population is growing 1.12% annually within five miles, households 1.25%, and average household income is projected up 15-18% by 2030. Under the demographics-to-rent lens, rising population and rising income together in a supply-constrained infill location is the strongest support in the portfolio for pushing rent on rollover.

upsideItems.item: A performing grocery anchor with very long control
upsideItems.detail: Key Foods ranks in the top 46% of its chain nationally by foot traffic (Placer.ai, TTM June 2026) and holds four 5-year options running to September 2054 - effectively permanent anchor stability underpinning the shop line and any phased redevelopment. The gross structure is the cost of that stability, not a reason to doubt it.

upsideItems.item: Contractual growth already signed across the shop roster
upsideItems.detail: Eleven leases carry contracted steps landing between December 2026 and May 2033 - T-Mobile, Golden Krust (five annual steps to $24.00), Experience the One, J-Lo Beauty Supply (five annual steps to $6.19), Key Foods (to $7.43 in 2029) and The Juice Bar (to $7.40 in 2027) among them. Growth on this portion arrives without leasing risk.

otherIncome.source: Rainbow co-tenancy percentage rent (4% of gross sales, both stores, in lieu of base rent)
otherIncome.note: NOT ordinary percentage rent - this is alternative rent paid because the co-tenancy clauses have been triggered. Flat $1,200 per year, not escalated in CBRE's model.
